profile.campus: Chicago metro, Illinois (Equinix Chicago campus, CH1-CH5 and CH7)
profile.reading:
Per Equinix own site, this CH7 facility is located at 111 Plaza Drive, Westmont, IL 60559 (DuPage County) and totals 29,289 sq ft. Redundancy: 2N Power redundancy (minimum cabinet density 2kVA), N+20% Cooling redundancy. No MW power capacity figure is published on this page. CH7 is Equinix's smallest disclosed Chicago-metro building by square footage, sited in the western DuPage County suburbs rather than the city's South Loop carrier-hotel corridor or the Elk Grove Village/O'Hare-adjacent industrial cluster where CH3 and several sibling buildings sit.

Equinix, the operator, was founded in 1998 by Al Avery and Jay Adelson and has grown into a global colocation and interconnection provider operating more than 260 data centers across over 70 metros worldwide; the company converted to a real estate investment trust (REIT) in 2015. Chicago is positioned by Equinix as the fourth-largest primary data center market in the US and a hub for its financial-services ecosystem, connecting trading firms, exchanges, and technology vendors via Equinix Fabric interconnection, cross-connects, and Equinix Cloud Exchange, alongside cloud on-ramps for AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle Cloud, and IBM Cloud.

CH7's DuPage County location, west of the city in Westmont, IL, places it in a different sub-market from the Cermak Road carrier-hotel corridor and the Elk Grove Village/O'Hare industrial cluster where sibling buildings CH1 and CH3 sit, giving Equinix a westward-suburban option within the same metro for customers seeking geographic diversity from the downtown core.

DuPage County's Westmont location gives Equinix a suburban option served by different electric utility infrastructure than the city-proper Cermak Road buildings, useful for customers seeking geographic and grid diversity within a single metro rather than pure latency-driven proximity to the Loop's financial exchanges; CH7's smaller footprint compared to CH1 and CH3 reflects its role as a supplementary rather than primary Chicago-metro site in Equinix's own facility lineup.

reading.body:
Equinix CH7 is a 29,289 square foot facility in Westmont, Illinois, west of Chicago's downtown carrier-hotel corridor. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this building, only a minimum cabinet density of 2 kilowatts per rack under 2N power redundancy. At that stated minimum density, the facility could host roughly 14,600 racks if fully utilized for IT load, though this represents a floor rather than a design target. The building's footprint places it among Equinix's smaller disclosed Chicago-metro sites.

CH7 operates under 2N power redundancy and N plus 20 percent cooling redundancy, qualifying it to host workloads requiring dual-fed power paths and headroom for thermal management. These specifications are standard for enterprise colocation rather than markers of capacity for high-density accelerator training. Illinois publishes MW capacity figures for only six of its 44 mapped data center facilities. CH7 does not appear in that published set, and Equinix does not disclose its power budget on the facility's specification page.

Within Illinois, this facility ranks 7th among the small number of sites with published power capacity but contributes no disclosed megawatts to the state's known total of 236 MW. CH7 serves Equinix's goal of geographic and grid diversity within the Chicago metro for enterprise and financial-services tenants rather than emerging as a primary venue for large-scale compute deployment. Whether the building matters to AI scaling depends entirely on tenant mix, which Equinix does not publish for this location.
